Peggy Flanagan

Democratic-Farmer-Labor candidate for U.S. Senator, Minnesota · Open seat

Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota

Peggy Flanagan is the Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) nominee for the U.S. Senate seat in Minnesota that is opening because Sen. Tina Smith is retiring. She has been Minnesota's lieutenant governor under Gov. Tim Walz since January 2019. Before that, she served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2015 to 2019.

Where Flanagan stands

Social Security
Wants to avoid benefit cuts by applying the Social Security payroll tax to earnings of $250,000 or more. Supports the Social Security Expansion Act and says it would keep the program solvent for at least seven decades.
Trade and tariffs
Says the current tariffs are hurting Minnesota industries, including soybean and corn growers. Argues tariffs are under the control of Congress and that Congress needs to act on them.
Immigration
Supports overhauling ICE and replacing it with a system she says would secure the border while providing due process and a pathway to citizenship for law-abiding long-term residents.
Israel and Gaza
Says she would not support additional offensive weapons or military aid to Israel while Benjamin Netanyahu leads its government. Calls the Hamas attack of Oct. 7, 2023, horrific and has previously described Israel's response in Gaza as genocide.
War in Iran
Has opposed U.S. military involvement in Iran from the start and says she would vote to end the war, citing its financial cost and U.S. service member deaths.
Abortion
Supported Minnesota's 2023 law guaranteeing access to reproductive health care, including abortion. Says she would interview Supreme Court nominees before deciding but does not expect to support Trump appointees.
Public-program fraud
Says Gov. Walz has taken responsibility for overseeing state programs where fraud occurred, and that her own role focused on other priorities such as paid family and medical leave and free school lunches.
Health care and wages
Pledged to support a labor-backed economic package that would raise the minimum wage, lower health care costs, and reduce corporate influence in Washington.
Term limits
Opposes term limits for U.S. senators and says voters can decide when a senator has served long enough.

Background

  • Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota, 2019–present
  • Minnesota House of Representatives, District 46A, 2015–2019
  • B.A., University of Minnesota
  • Citizen of the White Earth Nation
  • Born 1979 in St. Louis Park, Minnesota
